tier_reason: Manual page 11 (rendered screenshot) shows 'Printing speed: P7 trace: 5 210 000 per sec; Buffer: 688 000 per sec; Console: 10 000 per sec' on an Intel i7-870 dated 16.03.2015, and page 10 gives the 50 000 traces/s at 0.5% CPU and ~3.3 million/s max figures; the harness Tests/Speed/Speed.cpp is public and the CPU is named, but compiler and flags are never stated and the numbers are first-party, so C.

corrections.caveats: No head-to-head against any logging library (the manual never names spdlog, glog or log4cplus); the only baselines are printf and vsprintf. The P7 side is a call-site enqueue into a ring buffer drained by a background thread: in Tests/Speed/Speed.cpp the timer stops before the client is released, so delivery to the file is not timed, and it is not comparable to a synchronous console print. The buffer case formats 6 arguments with vsprintf ('[%s][%s][%d][%d][%d] ... iteration is %d') while the P7 trace call passes 1 argument (P7 captures file, function, line, thread and processor as binary metadata and defers formatting); the console case calls printf with the already formatted buffer as the format string, so it prints the previous line unformatted and without a newline, i.e. it times raw terminal output. The shipped Speed.cpp prints its results as text, while the page-11 figure plots 'To P7trace/To Buffer/To Console' counters (Count 1000) in the Baical viewer and quotes its Max column, so the 2015 screenshot came from a different build of the test. The page-10 figures (50 000 traces/s at 0.5% CPU, ~3.3 million/s max on i7-870) were measured with /P7.Sink=Baical over loopback, not to file. Compiler and flags are unstated; numbers are first-party and from 2015. The manual and Speed.cpp in CMakePorts/libp7-baical are byte-identical to the Faramax/libp7-baical mirror (a 0-star fork of Mixaill/libp7-baical). The upstream site baical.net was not reachable; the CMakePorts port's last commit was 2020-02-06 (v5.2.0) while upstream may have newer releases. Claim words on the list ('high-speed', 'minimal CPU and memory') match the manual's speed chapter.

notes: Numbers verified on the rendered page-11 figure and page-10 text; benchmark_url moved to the identical copy in the entry's own repo (cmake branch). Main shortcomings: only printf/vsprintf baselines, async enqueue timed against synchronous formatting and console output, unequal argument counts, figure from a different test build, compiler/flags unstated, abandoned since 2020. License LGPL-3.0-or-later confirmed from LICENSE.md and the 'version 3.0 ... or any later version' source headers.

tier_reason: The README feature list says verbatim 'high-performance, 250'000 logs/second on my laptop, about 1000 times faster than syslog(3) with rsyslogd' (repeated in doc/UsersGuide-EN.md) with no CPU, compiler, flags or syslog timing published; first-party numbers without methodology, and a >50x gain with unstated flags is capped at C anyway.

corrections.caveats: First-party sentence with no methodology: no CPU, compiler, flags, message size or rsyslogd configuration, and no published syslog timing anywhere in the repo (README, doc/UsersGuide-EN.md, doc/performence.txt). The repo ships load generators test/test_press_syslog.c and test/test_press_zlog.c; both log the 6-byte string 'loglog', but the syslog harness forks N processes that each call syslog(3) in a loop while the zlog harness forks processes that each run M threads, so the two sides are not symmetric. doc/performence.txt ('using makefile.linux for test, libzlog compile in O2') gives only zlog-vs-zlog and zlog-vs-direct-write timings (1 process x 10 threads x 100000 lines, 'time ./test_press_zlog 1 10 100000': v1.1.1 2.334s, v1.1.0 1.107s, v1.0.3 6.349s; direct write(2) test_press_write 1.872s), which suggests about 430k lines/s for v1.1.1 (derived from page data) and no syslog column; the User's Guide shows the same harness at 1.806s and slowing to 41.995s with an fsync period of 1K. The README's second claim, 'faster, safer and more powerful than log4c', has no numbers. The list entry tagged LGPL-2.1-only; the current repo is Apache-2.0 (LICENSE file and source headers such as src/zlog.h), so older releases may carry the older licence.

notes: Claim and metadata check out (Apache-2.0, 2.6k stars, 774 forks, last commit 2026-09-29, active). Main shortcomings: 1000x-vs-syslog figure is an unmeasured README sentence on an unnamed laptop, asymmetric press harnesses, no log4c numbers.
